citation: Papandreou D, Magriplis E, Abboud M et al. (2019). Consumption of Raw Orange, 100% Fresh Orange Juice, and Nectar- Sweetened Orange Juice—Effects on Blood Glucose and Insulin Levels on Healthy Subjects. Nutrients 11(9):2171.
protocol: Three orange products, randomised crossover 3 days apart, ~27 g total sugars each: two raw oranges (260 mL equivalent), 100% fresh orange juice (265 mL), nectar-sweetened orange juice (225 mL). Blood at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min.
population: n=20 non-diabetic young Emirati women, age 21.1 ± 0.9 y, BMI 23.6 ± 5.4 kg/m2 (13 normal weight, 7 overweight/obese; Table 2, mean (SD)).

reports.where: Table 3: serum glucose at 0, 30, 60, 90, 120 min per product, mean (SD)
Table 3: serum insulin at the same times per product

note: Paired-meal contrast, form: whole raw oranges vs fresh orange juice at matched sugars (sweetened nectar is a third arm). The cleanest liquid-against-solid pair found, with full time courses in a table. Watch: insulin units are not labelled in the table (fasting ~55, likely pmol/L, check the methods), fibre differs between whole fruit and juice, and the cohort includes 7 overweight women.
